claim: The Refusal redaction glossary entry describes RefusalRedactingRunner's WARNING logging exactly as the code behaves: the line includes the refusal's full text only when the refusal has no underlying cause or when the cause is another refusal, and the scope-analysis failure in safety/rls.py is logged nowhere.
source_excerpt: - **Refusal redaction** — While a rule-set file is configured, `RefusalRedactingRunner` replaces the text of every guard refusal with its kind and logs one WARNING line per refusal. That line includes the refusal's full text only when the refusal has no underlying cause, or when the cause is another refusal. Otherwise the redactor assumes the guard already logged the cause and leaves the text out. That assumption does not always hold: when scope analysis fails in `src/sqllens/safety/rls.py`, the full reason is not logged anywhere.
verify_against: RefusalRedactingRunner and _logged_by_guard in src/sqllens/rule_sets.py, and the RlsError raised by scope analysis in src/sqllens/safety/rls.py
verify_hint: Check `RefusalRedactingRunner` and `_logged_by_guard` in `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` (around lines 960-1016) against the scope-analysis `RlsError` raise in `src/sqllens/safety/rls.py` (around lines 265-273)
prior_evidence: RefusalRedactingRunner (rule_sets.py:983-1016) catches UnsafeSqlError and RlsError, so it covers every refusal type (RuleSetRefusal, WholeRowSelectError, RlsError), and it logs at WARNING. But the claim says it logs the full reason, and that fails for one path. When a refusal has a non-refusal __cause__, _logged_by_guard (971-980) assumes the guard already logged the cause, and line 1011 then logs only the kind fields (the exception text is dropped). rls.py:265-273 raises RlsError('could not analyze SQL scopes ...: {e}') from e when traverse_scope fails, and rls.py has no logger at all (grep 'logg' finds no match). That RlsError therefore reaches the redactor with a non-refusal cause, gets redacted to REDACTED_RLS, and its full reason is logged nowhere. The docstring at 984 and the glossary claim 'log the full reason at WARNING' for every refusal, so this case contradicts them. Also, RuleSetRefusal is re-raised unchanged (1002-1004) and its reason is logged by RuleSetGuardRunner (880), which is fine. Guard-internal errors get REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR (961), which is not a refusal kind.

claim: The Catalog check glossary entry describes check_catalog's scope as the code implements it: existence for every table and column a rule-set file names, a data-type check only for each `compare` column and each `owner_via` `link_user_column`, run by preflight at startup and by ensure_catalog_confirmed on a request until it has passed once.
source_excerpt: - **Catalog check** — `check_catalog` in `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py`: it checks that every table and column a rule-set file names exists in the MySQL database, and that each `compare` column and each `owner_via` `link_user_column` has a data type that fits its rule. Preflight runs it at startup, and `ensure_catalog_confirmed` runs it on a request until it has passed once. See [database-connectors/rule-sets.md](database-connectors/rule-sets.md).
verify_against: check_catalog and _catalog_reads in src/sqllens/rule_sets.py, plus preflight.probe_database/_check_rule_set_catalog and ensure_catalog_confirmed
verify_hint: Check `check_catalog` and `_catalog_reads` in `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` (around lines 1091-1190) and `_check_rule_set_catalog` in `src/sqllens/preflight.py`
prior_evidence: check_catalog (src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:1118-1190) does check that every listed table (BASE TABLE) and column exists, and it runs at startup via preflight.probe_database -> _check_rule_set_catalog (preflight.py:151-154, 166) when a rule-set file is configured on MySQL. But the type check is narrower than the glossary claims: only `typed` entries from _catalog_reads (rules_sets.py:1091-1100) are compared against DATA_TYPE (lines 1178-1186). Those are compare-rule columns, parent_rule compare columns, and owner_via link_user_column. Ordinary listed columns, predicate columns and link row/target columns are checked for existence only, with no type check. The glossary line (docs/internal/glossary.md:11) says every table and column exists 'with the expected type', which overstates this. The check_catalog docstring itself limits type checking to compare columns and link_user_column. The check also runs at request time via ensure_catalog_confirmed, not only at startup, which the glossary does not say.
